1. Platinum Rewards Card: Rebate Eligibility and Calcluation
   ID: doc_credit_cards_platinum_rewards_card_010
   Score: 47.8815
   Content: ## Eligibility for the Annual Fee Rebate

- The Platinum Rewards Card annual fee rebate is earned only if you meet the required monthly spending threshold in every month of your cardmember year.
- A single month below the threshold disqualifies you from receiving the rebate for that entire cardmember year; there is no partial or prorated rebate.
- If your first cardmember year’s annual fee is waived under a promotional offer, the rebate does not apply to that year. Eligibility begins with the next cardmember year in which the annual fee is billed.

## How the Monthly Calculation Window Works

- Start date: Your first monthly window begins on your account opening date.
- Refresh cadence: Each new monthly window begins on the same calendar day each month (the monthly anniversary of your account opening) and ends the day before the next monthly anniversary.
- Cardmember year: Your rebate evaluation covers 12 consecutive monthly windows, starting from your account opening date (or from the start of the first fee-billed cardmember year after any promotional waiver).
- Posting date rule: Only transactions that post within a given monthly window count toward that month’s threshold. Authorization dates do not control eligibility.

Here’s a concise summary of the important disclosure items you asked about and what to look for on the page. I stuck to what the application/disclosures typically cover and what the knowledge base calls out — if any language on your screen looks different or unclear, you can paste that non‑sensitive text here and I’ll explain it.

1) Credit‑check authorization
- The form will ask you to authorize a credit check as part of underwriting. That authorization is required to process your application.
- The disclosure should say whether the lender will perform a credit check and may identify the type (it will usually say “credit check” or “credit pull”). If it doesn’t state the type, you can look for wording indicating a credit bureau inquiry and I can help interpret it.
- If you’re concerned about the effect on your credit, check the line that describes the credit check and share that wording (not your SSN) so I can explain what it means for you.

2) E‑communications and e‑signature
- The disclosure will ask you to agree to receive electronic communications (statements, notices, disclosures) and to accept that your electronic signature is binding.
- Accepting means the bank will deliver legal notices electronically rather than by physical mail and that your e‑signature counts the same as a handwritten signature.
- If you prefer paper, look for an option or contact info in the disclosure that explains how to request paper delivery (some products let you opt out of e‑delivery).

3) Arbitration / dispute‑resolution language
- Many card agreements include an arbitration clause or other dispute‑resolution terms. Typical effects:
  - Requires arbitration instead of filing most disputes in court.
  - Often includes a waiver of class‑action rights (meaning you usually cannot bring a class lawsuit).
  - May provide a way to opt out of arbitration within a short period after acceptance (if an opt‑out is offered, the disclosure will describe how and the deadline).
- Read the arbitration paragraph and, if you want, paste that paragraph here (non‑sensitive text only). I’ll explain what it would mean in plain language and whether there’s an opt‑out process.

4) Other items to watch for (brief)
- Rates & fees summary: confirm the intro APR, ongoing APR, foreign‑transaction fee, and any fees called out.
- Income verification: because you’re self‑employed, the bank may request tax returns, 1099s, or bank statements after submission.
- Privacy & data sharing: there will be a notice about how your information is used/shared; if you want a plain‑English summary of any line, paste it here.

Next step
- If you’re ready to proceed, check the credit‑check consent box, the e‑communications/e‑signature consent, and then click Submit. Tell me when you click Submit and I’ll stay here to help with the immediate result or any follow‑up requests.
- Or, if any specific sentence or paragraph on your disclosures looks unclear, paste that non‑sensitive text here and I’ll explain it before you consent.
